"One who does not train for the sake of increasing or diminishing form, and does not train for the sake of increasing or diminishing feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness, does not train for the sake of grasping or abandoning form. Likewise, he does not train for the sake of grasping or abandoning feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness. He does not train for the sake of grasping any phenomenon at all; he does not train for the sake of arising, and does not train for the sake of ceasing. One who does not train for the sake of grasping any phenomenon, who does not train for the sake of arising or ceasing, does not train for the sake of grasping omniscience itself, and does not train for the sake of its arising or ceasing. A bodhisattva, a great being, who trains in this way trains in omniscience, and will truly emerge into omniscience."

Then the venerable Śāriputra spoke to the venerable Subhūti as follows: "Venerable Subhūti, a bodhisattva, a great being, who does not train for the sake of grasping any phenomenon at all, who does not train for the sake of arising, and does not train for the sake of ceasing, does not train for the sake of grasping omniscience itself, and does not train for the sake of its arising or ceasing. Venerable Subhūti, does a bodhisattva, a great being, who trains in this way train in omniscience, and will he truly emerge into omniscience?"

The venerable Subhūti replied: "Venerable Śāriputra, so it is, so it is. Venerable Śāriputra, a bodhisattva, a great being, who does not train for the sake of grasping any phenomenon at all, who does not train for the sake of arising, and does not train for the sake of ceasing, does not train for the sake of grasping omniscience itself, does not train for the sake of its arising or ceasing. He also does not train for the sake of grasping the qualities of a buddha, and does not train for the sake of their arising or ceasing. Venerable Śāriputra, a bodhisattva, a great being, who trains in this way trains in omniscience, and will truly emerge into omniscience."

Then Śakra, lord of the gods, spoke to the venerable Śāriputra as follows: "Noble Śāriputra, from what should a bodhisattva, a great being, seek the Perfection of Wisdom?"

Śāriputra said: "Kauśika, a bodhisattva, a great being, should seek the Perfection of Wisdom in the chapter of the venerable Subhūti."

When he had said this, Śakra, lord of the gods, spoke to the venerable Śāriputra as follows: "Noble Śāriputra, this exposition of the Perfection of Wisdom that the noble Subhūti gives: by whose power should it be understood, and by whose blessing should it be understood?"

The venerable Śāriputra said: "Kauśika, this exposition of the Perfection of Wisdom that the venerable Subhūti gives should be understood as the power of the Tathāgata. It should be understood as the blessing of the Tathāgata."

Then the venerable Subhūti spoke to Śakra, lord of the gods as follows: "Kauśika, you say, 'This exposition of the Perfection of Wisdom that the noble Subhūti gives: by whose power should it be understood, and by whose blessing should it be understood?' Kauśika, this exposition of the Perfection of Wisdom that I give should be understood as the power of the Tathāgata. It should be understood as the blessing of the Tathāgata.

"And Kauśika, as for your question, 'From what should a bodhisattva, a great being, seek the Perfection of Wisdom?': Kauśika, a bodhisattva, a great being, should not seek the Perfection of Wisdom in form, nor should it be sought apart from form. In the same way, it should not be sought in feeling, nor in perception, nor in formations, nor in consciousness, and it should not be sought apart from consciousness.

"Why is that? Kauśika, because form is not the Perfection of Wisdom, and apart from form there is no Perfection of Wisdom."

In the same way, feeling is not the Perfection of Wisdom, perception is not, the formations are not, and consciousness is not the Perfection of Wisdom; and apart from consciousness there is no Perfection of Wisdom."

When this had been said, Śakra, lord of the gods, spoke to the venerable Subhūti: "Noble Subhūti, this Perfection of Wisdom is a great perfection. Noble Subhūti, this Perfection of Wisdom is an immeasurable perfection. Noble Subhūti, this Perfection of Wisdom is a limitless perfection. Noble Subhūti, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection."

The elder Subhūti replied: "So it is, Kauśika, so it is. This Perfection of Wisdom is a great perfection. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is an immeasurable perfection. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a limitless perfection. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection.

"Why is that? Because form is great, Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a great perfection. In the same way, because feeling, perception, the formations, and consciousness are great, Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a great perfection.

"Because form is immeasurable, Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is an immeasurable perfection. In the same way, because feeling, perception, the formations, and consciousness are immeasurable, Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is an immeasurable perfection.

"Because form is limitless, Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a limitless perfection. In the same way, because feeling, perception, the formations, and consciousness are limitless, Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a limitless perfection.

"Because form is unending, Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection. In the same way, because feeling, perception, the formations, and consciousness are unending, Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection.

"Kauśika, one does not become fixated on the idea of a 'great perfection.' In the same way, one does not become fixated on the idea of an 'immeasurable perfection,' nor on the idea of a 'limitless perfection,' nor on the idea of an 'unending perfection.'

"Therefore, Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a great perfection. It is an immeasurable perfection. It is a limitless perfection. Kauśika, it is an unending perfection.

"Kauśika, because the objects of focus are unending, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection. Kauśika, because sentient beings are unending, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection.

"And, Kauśika, in what way is it that, because the objects of focus are unending, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection?"

"Kauśika, it is like this: the beginning, middle, and end of all phenomena cannot be apprehended. Therefore, Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection. In this way, Kauśika, because the objects of focus are unending, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection.

"Furthermore, Kauśika, because all phenomena are unending and without limit, and because no beginning, middle, or end of them can be apprehended, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection. And why is this so? Kauśika, no beginning, middle, or end of form can be apprehended. Likewise, Kauśika, no beginning, middle, or end of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness can be apprehended. Thus, Kauśika, in this way too, because the objects of focus are unending, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection.

"Furthermore, Kauśika, sentient beings are unending and without limit. And why is this so? No beginning, middle, or end of sentient beings can be apprehended. Therefore, Kauśika, because sentient beings are unending, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection."

Then Śakra, lord of the gods (Indra), said this to the venerable Subhūti: "Noble Subhūti, in what way is it that, because sentient beings are unending, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection?"

The elder Subhūti replied: "Kauśika, it is because sentient beings are unending, being beyond any reckoning, or because they are reckoned as numberless, that this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection."

Śakra said: "Noble Subhūti, then how is it that, because sentient beings are unending, this Perfection of Wisdom is called an unending perfection?"

The elder Subhūti replied: "Kauśika, what do you think? The words 'sentient being, sentient being' are a designation for which phenomenon?"

Śakra said: "Noble Subhūti, these words 'sentient being, sentient being' are neither a designation for a phenomenon nor a designation for the absence of a phenomenon. This is a name that has been imputed, something that arose adventitiously. This imputed name has no real entity. This imputed name has nothing that belongs to a self. This imputed name 'sentient being, sentient being' is something that cannot be apprehended."

The elder Subhūti said: "Kauśika, what do you think? Is there any sentient being who has been established as such?"

Śakra said: "Noble Subhūti, there is not."

Subhūti said: "Kauśika, where no sentient being has been established, can there be unending sentient beings? Kauśika, suppose a Tathāgata, an arhat, a perfectly complete buddha were to remain for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges, and with a profound voice and speech that makes known what lies beyond all limits, were to utter the words 'sentient being, sentient being.' Would any sentient being thereby be born, or come to be born, or be taking birth, or cease, or come to cease, or be ceasing?"

Śakra said: "Noble Subhūti, no. And why is this so? Because sentient beings are pure from the very beginning, and thoroughly pure from the very beginning."

Subhūti said: "Kauśika, in this way too, because sentient beings are unending, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unending perfection."

Kauśika, in this way too, because sentient beings are limitless, this Perfection of Wisdom should be known as limitless.

Then the gods, together with Indra, together with Brahmā, together with the lords of beings, together with the sages, together with the assembly of men and women, three times cried out in joyous exclamation: "Wondrous! The Dharma! Wondrous! The Dharma! Wondrous! The Dharma! The very nature of phenomena, the arising of the Tathāgata, has been well spoken by the noble elder Subhūti, and he has declared, shown, expounded, and established it.

Blessed One, from this day forth, we will hold that those bodhisattvas, great beings, who are not separated from this Perfection of Wisdom, and those bodhisattvas, great beings, who abide in this abiding of the Perfection of Wisdom, that this abiding is the Tathāgata himself."

Then the Blessed One spoke to those gods, together with Indra, together with Brahmā, together with the lords of beings, together with the sages, together with that assembly of men and women: "Sons of the gods, so it is, so it is. Sons of the gods, when I was in the midst of the market of the royal city called Dīpavatī, in the presence of the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly awakened buddha Dīpaṃkara, I was never separated from this Perfection of Wisdom. At that time the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly awakened buddha Dīpaṃkara prophesied my unsurpassed, perfect awakening, saying: 'Young brahmin, in a future age, after countless eons, you will become the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly awakened buddha named Śākyamuni, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the buddha, the Blessed One.'"

Then those sons of the gods said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, it is wondrous that this Perfection of Wisdom of bodhisattvas, great beings, brings about, and sustains them, all the way to omniscience. Sugata, it is truly wondrous."

Thus ends the second chapter, called "Śakra," of the noble Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines.

The Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines, the third bundle.

Then the Blessed One knew which sons of the gods had gathered and were seated in that assembly, and which assembly of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen had gathered and were seated. Knowing that those sons of the gods had gathered and were seated, and knowing too that all four assemblies had gathered and were seated, he called as witnesses the sons of the gods who move in the desire realm and in the form realm, the sons of the gods of the Brahmā realm, and the sons of the gods of Luminosity, of Lesser Virtue, and of Akaniṣṭha. And he spoke to the sons of the gods who move in the desire realm, headed by Śakra, lord of the gods, to the sons of the gods of the Brahmā realm, headed by Mahābrahmā, and to the sons of the gods of Luminosity:

"Sons of the gods, if any son or daughter of good family holds, bears, reads, fully understands, or recites this Perfection of Wisdom, then Māra, or gods of Māra's retinue, who watch for an opening and seek an opening, will not find an opening. Sons of the gods, humans or non-humans who watch for an opening and seek an opening will not find an opening against that son or daughter of good family either."

Moreover, that son or daughter of good family will not die an untimely death, and will not do so without having first abandoned the faults of body and speech.

Sons of the gods, furthermore, those sons of the gods who have truly set out toward unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, and those sons of the gods who have not held, borne, read, fully understood, or recited this Perfection of Wisdom, will wish to come into the presence of that son of good family. They will listen to that son of good family who holds, bears, reads, fully understands, and recites this Perfection of Wisdom; and having heard it, they too will come to hold it, bear it, read it, fully understand it, and recite it.

Sons of the gods, furthermore, whether that son or daughter of good family who holds, bears, reads, fully understands, and recites the Perfection of Wisdom goes to a forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty house, or to an open place without shelter, or goes upon a road, or strays from the road, or goes into a wilderness, or into the great ocean; and whether going, walking, sitting, or lying down in this place or that, no fear and no stiffening of terror will arise or occur in them.

Then the four great kings spoke to the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, it is wonderful that the son or daughter of good family who comes to hold, bear, read, fully understand, and recite this Perfection of Wisdom thereby trains beings through the three vehicles, and yet does not give rise to the notion of a being. Blessed One, we shall guard, protect, and shelter that son or daughter of good family who comes to hold, bear, read, fully understand, and recite this Perfection of Wisdom."

Then Śakra, lord of the gods, spoke to the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, I too shall guard, protect, and shelter those sons or daughters of good family who come to hold, bear, read, fully understand, and recite this Perfection of Wisdom."

Then Brahmā, lord of the Sahā world-system, together with the sons of the gods of the Brahmā realm, also spoke to the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, we too shall guard, protect, and shelter that son or daughter of good family who comes to hold, bear, read, fully understand, and recite this Perfection of Wisdom."

Then Śakra, lord of the gods, spoke to the Blessed One once more: "Blessed One, it is wonderful that the son or daughter of good family who holds, bears, reads, fully understands, and recites this Perfection of Wisdom will certainly obtain these qualities in this very life and will be fully embraced by them. Blessed One, then, when one holds this Perfection of Wisdom, are all six perfections held?"

When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One said to Śakra, lord of the gods: "Kauśika, so it is. So it is. Kauśika, by holding the Perfection of Wisdom, all six perfections are held."

Kauśika, furthermore, if a son or daughter of good family holds, bears, reads, fully understands, and recites this Perfection of Wisdom, listen well to all the qualities that such a person will come to hold in this very life, and keep them in mind. I shall explain them to you.

Śakra, lord of the gods, said to the Blessed One, "Excellent!" and listened as the Blessed One had instructed. And the Blessed One spoke thus:

Kauśika, whoever wishes to quarrel with this Dharma, to oppose it, or to contradict it, their quarrels, oppositions, and contradictions, though they arise, will subside again and will not endure. The intentions of those who wish to quarrel, to oppose, and to contradict will not be fulfilled.

Why is this so? Kauśika, it comes about in this way. When a son or daughter of good family holds, bears, reads, fully understands, recites, teaches, explains, expounds, and memorizes this Perfection of Wisdom, whatever grounds for dispute arise against them will subside again and will not endure. The intentions of those who wish to quarrel, to oppose, and to contradict will not be fulfilled.

Kauśika, a son or daughter of good family who holds, bears, reads, fully understands, recites, teaches, explains, expounds, and memorizes this Perfection of Wisdom will also come to hold these further qualities in this very life.

Kauśika, it is like this. Suppose there is a plant called rtsi ma ghi, which thoroughly pacifies all poisons. Now a venomous snake, hungry and seeking food, sees some living creature. Wishing to eat it, the snake follows the scent of that creature and pursues it. Then the creature goes to the place where the rtsi ma ghi grows and settles there. And the snake, at the mere scent of that plant, turns back. Why is that? The overpowering of the snake's venom should be seen as the medicinal power of that plant. So great is the potency of that plant.

In the same way, Kauśika, for a son or daughter of good family who holds, bears, reads, fully understands, recites, teaches, explains, expounds, and memorizes this Perfection of Wisdom, whatever grounds for dispute, opposition, and contradiction arise are quickly brought to nothing, right where they stand, by the majesty, strength, and power of the Perfection of Wisdom and by the strength that the Perfection of Wisdom generates. They are pacified and do not increase. Wherever they arose, right there they cease and vanish, and they do not endure.

Why is this so? Because the Perfection of Wisdom pacifies all clinging, from attachment and the rest up to nirvāṇa itself; it does not cause it to grow.

Kauśika, the Four Great Kings, Śakra, lord of the gods, Brahmā, lord of this world, the buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and all the bodhisattvas as well,

Kauśika, any son or daughter of good family who holds, bears in mind, reads, thoroughly understands, recites, teaches, explains, expounds, and memorizes this Perfection of Wisdom will be protected, defended, and sheltered. In this very life they will come to be endowed with these good qualities.

Furthermore, Kauśika, any son or daughter of good family who holds, bears in mind, reads, thoroughly understands, recites, teaches, explains, expounds, and memorizes this Perfection of Wisdom will have words worthy of being taken to heart. Their words will be gentle, fitting, and free of disorder. They will not be overpowered by anger, nor overpowered by pride.

Why is this so? Because the Perfection of Wisdom thoroughly tames them, and the Perfection of Wisdom thoroughly humbles them. So they do not let anger grow, and they do not let pride grow. They do not hold resentment, they do not harbor malice, and they do not let latent tendencies take hold.

Son or daughter of good family, in one who lives in this way, mindfulness and loving-kindness will arise. Such a one thinks: "If I were to give rise to malice, my faculties would be disturbed and the color of my face would change. I have properly entered upon unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening and wish to train in this. It is not fitting for me to fall under the power of anger." And so they quickly regain mindfulness.

Kauśika, any son or daughter of good family who comes to hold, bear in mind, read, thoroughly understand, recite, teach, explain, expound, and memorize this Perfection of Wisdom will also take hold of these good qualities in this very life.

When the Blessed One had spoken thus, Śakra, lord of the gods, said to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, it is wonderful how this Perfection of Wisdom abides for the sake of the bodhisattvas, the great beings, being thoroughly tamed and free of arrogance."

The Blessed One declared: "Furthermore, Kauśika, suppose a son or daughter of good family comes to hold, bear in mind, read, thoroughly understand, recite, teach, explain, expound, and memorize this Perfection of Wisdom. Suppose such a one, because of holding, bearing in mind, reading, thoroughly understanding, reciting, teaching, explaining, expounding, and memorizing this Perfection of Wisdom, were to be the first to enter the battle when armies clash. Whether they are entering the battlefield, have entered it, have passed beyond it, or are walking, standing, or sitting within the battlefield, Kauśika, that a son or daughter of good family who keeps in mind, holds, reads, thoroughly understands, recites, teaches, explains, expounds, or memorizes this Perfection of Wisdom should meet with a danger to life is impossible and cannot happen. That they should meet with a danger to life through harm done by others is likewise impossible."

Kauśika, furthermore, if someone were to hurl a stick, a weapon, a clod of earth, or anything else at such a person, it would not strike their body. Why is that? Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a great knowledge-mantra (vidyā). Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is an immeasurable knowledge-mantra. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a boundless knowledge-mantra. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unsurpassed knowledge-mantra. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unequaled knowledge-mantra. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is the knowledge-mantra that equals the unequaled.

Why is that? Kauśika, a son or daughter of good family who trains in this knowledge-mantra does not think of harming themselves, does not think of harming others, and does not think of harming both.

Kauśika, a bodhisattva, a great being, who trains in this knowledge-mantra will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening and will attain the wisdom of omniscience. Having become fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, they will behold the minds of all sentient beings. Why is that? Kauśika, for a bodhisattva, a great being, who has trained in this knowledge-mantra, there is nothing that is unattained, unknown, or not made directly evident. Therefore it is called the wisdom of omniscience.

Kauśika, a son or daughter of good family who keeps in mind, holds, reads, thoroughly understands, recites, teaches, explains, expounds, and memorizes this Perfection of Wisdom will, in this very life, also take hold of this excellent quality.

Kauśika, furthermore, suppose that in some place this Perfection of Wisdom is written down in a small form and made into a book, and is set down with offerings made beforehand and is honored and revered, but one does not keep it in mind, hold it, read it, thoroughly understand it, recite it, teach it, explain it, expound it, or memorize it. Even there, Kauśika, apart from the ripening of previous karma, humans and non-humans who watch for an opening will not find an opening, even if they look for one. That is impossible. Kauśika, that son or daughter of good family will, in this very life, also take hold of this excellent quality.

Kauśika, it is just like this. Consider those who sit at the heart of awakening, who sit around the heart of awakening, who sit within the heart of awakening, or who sit at the foot of the tree of awakening, whether humans, non-humans, or even animals. Apart from the ripening of previous karma, humans and non-humans cannot oppress them, harm them, or bring them down. Why is that? Because the Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly complete buddhas of the past, the future, and the present, who cultivate and teach fearlessness, freedom from enmity, and freedom from terror toward all sentient beings, have fully awakened there, are fully awakening there, and will fully awaken there, to complete awakening.

In the same way, Kauśika, wherever a son or daughter of good family upholds, retains, reads, masters, recites, teaches, explains, expounds, and memorizes this very Perfection of Wisdom, there, Kauśika, apart from the ripening of previous karma, sentient beings, whether human or non-human, cannot oppress them, harm them, or bring them down. Why is that? Kauśika, it is because this very Perfection of Wisdom has made that place a shrine for beings, a place to be honored, venerated, worshiped, adorned, attended, respected, and treated as a teacher, and has made it a protector, a refuge, a dwelling, and a support for those beings who come to it. Kauśika, that son or daughter of good family also receives these benefits in this very life.

When the Blessed One had spoken thus, Śakra, lord of the gods (Indra), said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, suppose one son or daughter of good family writes out this Perfection of Wisdom, puts it into book form, and keeps it, and honors it, respects it, treats it as a teacher, venerates it, worships it, adorns it, and attends it with divine flowers, divine incense, divine fragrances, divine garlands, divine unguents, divine powders, divine garments, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and divine pennants, with rows of divine lamps all around, and with many kinds of divine offerings. And suppose another receives and keeps the relics of the Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly complete buddhas who have passed into final nirvāṇa, placed within a stūpa, and likewise honors, respects, treats as teachers, venerates, worships, adorns, and attends them with divine flowers, divine incense, divine fragrances, divine garlands, divine unguents, divine powders, divine garments, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and divine pennants, with rows of divine lamps all around, and with many kinds of divine offerings. Of these two sons or daughters of good family, which one would generate the greater merit?"

When he had said this, the Blessed One spoke to Śakra, lord of the gods, as follows: "Kauśika, in that case I shall question you in turn, and you should answer as best you can. Kauśika, what do you think? That which is the realization of the very substance of the omniscience of the Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly complete buddhas, by training in which path did the Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly complete buddhas attain unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening and omniscience, and become fully and completely awakened?"

When he had said this, Śakra, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, it was by training in this very Perfection of Wisdom that the Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly complete buddhas attained unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening and omniscience, and became fully and completely awakened."

The Blessed One said:

"Therefore, Kauśika, it is not by obtaining this physical body of mine that one is counted as a Tathāgata. It is by obtaining omniscience that one is counted as a Tathāgata. Kauśika, the omniscience of the Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly complete buddhas, arises from the Perfection of Wisdom. And this physical body of the Tathāgata, which has been obtained, also arises from the Perfection of Wisdom together with skillful means, for it has become the support of omniscient wisdom.

"Relying on this support, omniscient wisdom is made manifest. The body of the Buddha is made manifest as well. The body of the Dharma is made manifest, and the body of the Saṅgha is made manifest. Thus, since this physical body, obtained as the cause of omniscient wisdom, has become the support of omniscient wisdom, it becomes a shrine for all beings. It becomes an object of homage, reverence, and honor as one's teacher, an object of veneration, of offering, of adornment, and of devoted service. In the same way, even after I have passed completely beyond sorrow, offerings will be made to those relics as well.

"Therefore, Kauśika, suppose some son or daughter of good family were to write out this Perfection of Wisdom, place it in a book, and keep it. And suppose they were to honor it with divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine unguents, divine powders, divine garments, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and divine pennants, and with divine rows of lamps all around, and with many kinds of divine offerings; and were to revere it, honor it as a teacher, venerate it, make offerings to it, adorn it, and serve it devotedly. Kauśika, those sons or daughters of good family would generate a very great deal of merit. Why is that? Because that son or daughter of good family will have made an offering to omniscient wisdom.

"But if a son or daughter of good family were to ask about this Perfection of Wisdom, and were to revere, honor as a teacher, venerate, make offerings to, adorn, and devotedly serve this very Perfection of Wisdom set down in a book, offering it many kinds of offerings, they would generate even more merit than the former. Why is that? Kauśika, because whoever makes offerings to the Perfection of Wisdom makes offerings to omniscient wisdom."

When the Blessed One had said this, Śakra, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, those people in this Jambudvīpa who do not ask about this Perfection of Wisdom, do not hold it, do not bear it in mind, do not read it, do not fully comprehend it, do not recite it aloud, do not teach it, do not explain it, do not give its transmission, and do not memorize it; who do not honor this Perfection of Wisdom with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, unguents, powders, garments, parasols, banners, bells, and pennants, with rows of lamps all around, and with many kinds of offerings; who do not revere it, do not honor it as a teacher, do not venerate it, do not make offerings to it, do not adorn it, and do not serve it devotedly..."

Blessed One, did you not understand that making offerings to the Perfection of Wisdom taught by the Blessed One is of such great meaning? Blessed One, did you not realize that making offerings to this Perfection of Wisdom taught by the Blessed One is endowed with such great benefit? Did you not know that its fruit is so great and its karmic ripening so great? Or, though you understood, realized, and knew it, did you nonetheless lack faith?

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke to Śakra, lord of the gods (Indra), saying: "Kauśika, what do you think? Among the people of Jambudvīpa, how many are there who have understood the Buddha and are endowed with faith, who have understood the Dharma and are endowed with faith, and who have understood the Saṅgha and are endowed with faith?"

When the Blessed One had spoken thus, Śakra, lord of the gods, said to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, among the people of Jambudvīpa, those who have understood the Buddha and are endowed with faith, who have understood the Dharma and are endowed with faith, and who have understood the Saṅgha and are endowed with faith are few."

When he had said this, the Blessed One spoke to Śakra, lord of the gods: "Kauśika, so it is, so it is. Among the people of Jambudvīpa, those who have understood the Buddha and are endowed with faith, who have understood the Dharma and are endowed with faith, and who have understood the Saṅgha and are endowed with faith are few.

"Kauśika, those who have attained the fruit of stream-entry are few, yet even fewer than these are those who have attained the fruit of once-returner and the fruit of non-returner. Fewer still than these are those who have attained arhatship. Fewer still are those who realize solitary awakening. Fewer still are those who give rise to the mind of unsurpassable, perfect, complete awakening. Fewer still are those who, having given rise to the mind of unsurpassable, perfect, complete awakening, bring that awakening mind to full growth. Fewer still are those who, having given rise to the mind of unsurpassable, perfect, complete awakening and brought it to full growth, abide exerting diligence. Fewer still are those who apply themselves to the Perfection of Wisdom. Fewer still are those who practice the Perfection of Wisdom. Fewer still are those who, practicing the Perfection of Wisdom and striving in it, abide on the irreversible bodhisattva ground. Fewer still are those who, practicing the Perfection of Wisdom and striving in it, come to manifestly and completely awaken to unsurpassable, perfect, complete awakening. Fewer still are those who, practicing the Perfection of Wisdom and striving in it, have actually become fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfect, complete awakening.

"Kauśika, there are great bodhisattvas who abide on the irreversible bodhisattva ground and have become fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfect, complete awakening. And when sons and daughters of good family, possessed of excellent superior intention, train and strive in the Perfection of Wisdom, those buddhas teach this Perfection of Wisdom to others, give them prophecy, and also lead them to take hold of it, and..."

and cause them to hold it, to read it, to fully comprehend it, to recite it, to teach it, to explain it, to give transmission of it, and to memorize it. And such beings are those who honor the Perfection of Wisdom with divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine ointments, divine powders, divine garments, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and divine flags, and all around with divine rows of lamps, and with many kinds of divine offerings. They revere it, hold it as their teacher, make gains for it, make offerings to it, adorn it with fine decoration, and attend upon it with respect.

"Moreover, Kauśika, there are immeasurable, innumerable beings who give rise to the awakening mind, and having given rise to the awakening mind, enlarge the awakening mind, and having fully enlarged the awakening mind, practice for the sake of awakening. Yet, Kauśika, of those immeasurable, innumerable beings who practice for awakening, perhaps only one or two come to abide on the irreversible bodhisattva ground. Why is that? Kauśika, unsurpassable, perfect, complete awakening is hard to accomplish for those of feeble diligence, for the lazy, for those of lowly thought, lowly mind, lowly perception, lowly inclination, and lowly wisdom.

"Therefore, Kauśika, any son or daughter of good family who wishes to become fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfect, complete awakening quickly and with ease should, without interruption, listen to this very Perfection of Wisdom, take hold of it, hold it, read it, fully comprehend it, recite it, teach it, explain it, give transmission of it, memorize it, and inquire into it thoroughly. Why is that? Kauśika, those sons or daughters of good family should think thus: 'When the Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened buddhas of the past were practicing the conduct of bodhisattvas, they trained in this very Perfection of Wisdom in this way. So we too shall train in it.' They should understand: 'This Perfection of Wisdom is our Teacher.' For, Kauśika, whether the Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened buddhas remain or have passed into complete nirvāṇa, great bodhisattvas must rely on this very Perfection of Wisdom.

"Therefore, Kauśika, suppose some son or daughter of good family, in order to honor a Tathāgata, arhat, perfectly awakened buddha who has passed into complete nirvāṇa, were to have made many millions of stūpas, made of the seven precious substances and containing the relics of the Tathāgata as their essence. And having made them, for as long as they lived they were to honor them with divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine ointments, divine powders, divine garments, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and divine flags, and all around with divine rows of lamps, and with many kinds of divine offerings, revering them, holding them as their teacher, making gains for them, making offerings to them, adorning them with fine decoration, and attending upon them with respect. Kauśika, what do you think? Would that son or daughter of good family generate much merit on that basis?"

Śakra (Indra) replied:

"Blessed One, it would be much. Sugata, it would be much."

The Blessed One declared: "Kauśika, yet this son or daughter of good family generates far more merit than that. Whoever has faith in this Perfection of Wisdom, reflects on it, is devoted to it, and, with a clear and confident mind, has generated the awakening mind; and who, with superior intention, listens to it, upholds it, bears it in mind, recites it, comprehends it thoroughly, reads it aloud, teaches it, explains it closely, gives its transmission, memorizes it, and also teaches it extensively and correctly to others; who explains its meaning, contemplates it with the mind, and examines it here with wisdom in accord with how it is established; and who does so thinking, 'May the lineage of the buddhas not be cut off, and may the sacred Dharma not vanish,' and thereby makes the sacred Dharma endure for a long time; and who, never separated from this approach, accomplishes benefit for the bodhisattvas, the great beings; who, even if it is only a short text, has it set down in a book and holds it, or places it in a shrine, and honors that Perfection of Wisdom with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, garments, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, and all around with rows of lamps and many kinds of offerings; who reveres it, holds it as a teacher, makes gains for it, makes offerings to it, adorns it with fine decoration, and attends upon it with respect. Kauśika, this very son or daughter of good family generates a far greater mass of merit than that.

"Kauśika, let alone many millions of stūpas made of the seven precious substances and containing relics of the Tathāgata. Kauśika, suppose some son or daughter of good family were to have this entire Jambudvīpa filled with stūpas made of the seven precious substances, containing relics of the Tathāgata. And having done so, for as long as they lived they were to honor them with divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine ointments, divine powders, divine garments, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and divine flags, and all around with divine rows of lamps, and with many kinds of divine offerings, revering them, holding them as their teacher, making gains for them, making offerings to them, adorning them with fine decoration, and attending upon them with respect. Kauśika, what do you think? Would that son or daughter of good family generate much merit on that basis?"

Śakra (Indra) replied: "Blessed One, it would be much. Sugata, it would be much."

The Blessed One declared: "Kauśika, yet this son or daughter of good family generates far more merit than that. Whoever has faith in this Perfection of Wisdom, reflects on it, is devoted to it, and, with a clear and confident mind, has generated the awakening mind; and who, with superior intention, listens to it, upholds it, bears it in mind, recites it, comprehends it thoroughly, reads it aloud, teaches it, explains it closely, gives its transmission, memorizes it, and also teaches it extensively and correctly to others; who explains its meaning, contemplates it with the mind, and examines it here with wisdom in accord with how it is established; and who does so thinking, 'May the lineage of the buddhas not be cut off, and may the sacred Dharma not vanish,' and thereby makes the sacred Dharma endure for a long time;"

and who, not departing from the proper way, does what benefits bodhisattvas, the great beings; who writes this Perfection of Wisdom in a small scroll or book and keeps it, or places it respectfully, and honors it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, and with rows of lamps all around, and with many kinds of offerings; who shows it reverence, treats it as a teacher, esteems it, makes offerings to it, adorns it with fine decoration, and attends upon it with respect: this son or daughter of good family generates far greater merit than that.

Kauśika, let alone this Jambudvīpa filled with stūpas that are made of the seven precious substances and contain the relics of the Tathāgatas. Kauśika, suppose that all the beings who dwell in a world system of the four great continents were each made to build a stūpa of the seven precious substances containing the relics of the Tathāgatas. And suppose that, for as long as they lived, they honored those stūpas with divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine unguents, divine powders, divine robes, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and divine flags, and with rows of divine lamps all around, and with many kinds of divine offerings; and showed them reverence, treated them as teachers, esteemed them, made offerings to them, adorned them with fine decoration, and attended upon them with respect. Kauśika, what do you think? Would all those beings generate great merit on that basis?

Śakra (Indra) replied: Blessed One, they would generate much. Sugata, they would generate much.

The Blessed One declared: Kauśika, even more merit than that is generated by this son or daughter of good family who has clear faith in this Perfection of Wisdom, who reflects on it and is inclined toward it with a serene mind, who has generated the awakening mind, and who, with superior intention, listens to it, upholds it, bears it in mind, reads it, comprehends it thoroughly, recites it aloud, teaches it, explains it closely, gives its transmission, and memorizes it; who also teaches it extensively and correctly to others, explains its meaning, contemplates it with the mind, and examines it here with wisdom in accord with how it is established; who does so thinking, "May the lineage of the buddhas not be cut off, and may the sacred Dharma not vanish," and thereby makes the sacred Dharma endure for a long time; and who, not departing from the proper way, does what benefits bodhisattvas, the great beings; who writes this Perfection of Wisdom in a small scroll or book and keeps it, or places it respectfully, and honors it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, and with rows of lamps all around, and with many kinds of offerings; who shows it reverence, treats it as a teacher, esteems it, makes offerings to it, adorns it with fine decoration, and attends upon it with respect: this son or daughter of good family generates far greater merit on that basis.

Kauśika, let alone all the beings of a world system of the four great continents. Kauśika, suppose that all the beings who dwell in a thousandfold world system were each made to build a stūpa of the seven precious substances containing the relics of the Tathāgatas.

And suppose that for as long as they lived, these beings were to honor those stūpas with divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine unguents, divine powders, divine garments, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and divine flags, and with divine rows of lamps all around, and with many kinds of divine offerings; and suppose they showed them reverence, treated them as a teacher, esteemed them, made offerings to them, adorned them with fine decoration, and attended upon them with respect. Kauśika, what do you think? Would all those beings generate much merit on that basis?

Śakra (Indra) replied: Blessed One, it would be much. Sugata, it would be much.

The Blessed One declared: Kauśika, a son or daughter of good family generates far greater merit than that. This is the one who has faith in this Perfection of Wisdom, who considers it and inclines toward it, whose mind is clear and confident, and who, having generated the mind of awakening, with a superior intention listens to it, upholds it, retains it, reads it, comprehends it fully, recites it, teaches it, instructs others in it, gives its transmission, memorizes it, and expounds it extensively and correctly to others as well. Such a one explains its meaning, reflects on it with the mind, and examines it thoroughly with the wisdom that has been attained. Thinking, "May the lineage of the buddhas not be cut off; may the sacred Dharma not vanish," that person makes the sacred Dharma endure for a long time. Not departing from the proper way, that person accomplishes benefit for the bodhisattvas, the great beings. Or, if it is a small version, that person has it written down in a book and keeps it, or places it somewhere, and honors that Perfection of Wisdom with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, unguents, powders, garments, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, and with rows of lamps all around, and with many kinds of offerings; shows it reverence, treats it as a teacher, esteems it, makes offerings to it, adorns it with fine decoration, and attends upon it with respect. Kauśika, that son or daughter of good family generates far greater merit on that basis.

Kauśika, let alone all the beings of a thousandfold world system. Kauśika, consider also the beings in the middle, twofold thousandfold world system, however many there may be. Suppose that each and every one of them were made to build a stūpa of the seven precious substances, each with the relics of the Tathāgatas as its core. And suppose that for as long as they lived, they were to honor those stūpas with divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine unguents, divine powders, divine garments, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and divine flags, and with divine rows of lamps all around, and with many kinds of divine offerings; and suppose they showed them reverence, treated them as a teacher, esteemed them, made offerings to them, adorned them with fine decoration, and attended upon them with respect. Kauśika, what do you think? Would all those beings generate much merit on that basis?

Śakra replied: Blessed One, it would be much. Sugata, it would be much.

The Blessed One declared: Kauśika, a son or daughter of good family generates far greater merit than that. This is the one who has faith in this Perfection of Wisdom, who considers it and inclines toward it, whose mind is clear and confident, and who, having generated the mind of awakening,

with superior intention listens to it, holds it, bears it in mind, reads it, comprehends it, recites it, teaches it, expounds it closely, gives its transmission, memorizes it, and also explains it widely and rightly to others, who unravels its meaning, reflects upon it with the mind, and examines it thoroughly with wisdom, as it is truly established; who, thinking, "May the lineage of the buddhas not be cut off; may the sacred Dharma not vanish," works to make the sacred Dharma endure for a long time; and who, in a way that is not divorced from the proper manner, brings about benefit for the bodhisattvas, the great beings. And if, even in small measure, such a person has it set down in a book and keeps it, or places it in a shrine, and makes offerings to that Perfection of Wisdom with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, with rings of lamps all around, and with many kinds of offerings, showing reverence, treating it as a teacher, esteeming it, making offerings to it, adorning it, and attending upon it with respect, then, Kauśika, that son or daughter of good family generates, on that basis alone, extremely great merit.

Kauśika, set aside all the beings of a middle world system of two thousand worlds. Kauśika, consider also all the beings there are in the world system of the great trichiliocosm, the three-thousandfold great thousand. Suppose each one of those beings were made to build a stūpa made of the seven precious substances, each containing relics of the Tathāgata at its heart. And suppose that for as long as they lived, they made offerings to those stūpas with divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine ointments, divine powders, divine robes, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and divine flags, with rings of divine lamps all around, and with many kinds of divine offerings, showing reverence, treating them as a teacher, esteeming them, making offerings to them, adorning them, and attending upon them with respect. Kauśika, what do you think? Would all those beings generate much merit on that basis?

Śakra replied: Blessed One, it would be much. Sugata, it would be much.

The Blessed One declared: Kauśika, a son or daughter of good family generates far greater merit than that. This is the one who has faith in this Perfection of Wisdom, who considers it and inclines toward it, whose mind is clear and confident, and who, having generated the mind of awakening, with superior intention listens to it, holds it, bears it in mind, reads it, comprehends it, recites it, teaches it, expounds it closely, gives its transmission, memorizes it, and also explains it widely and rightly to others, who unravels its meaning, reflects upon it with the mind, and examines it thoroughly with wisdom, as it is truly established; who, thinking, "May the lineage of the buddhas not be cut off; may the sacred Dharma not vanish," works to make the sacred Dharma endure for a long time; and who, in a way that is not divorced from the proper manner, brings about benefit for the bodhisattvas, the great beings. And if, even in small measure, such a person has it set down in a book and keeps it, or places it in a shrine, and makes offerings to that Perfection of Wisdom with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, with rings of lamps all around, and with many kinds of offerings, showing reverence, treating it as a teacher, esteeming it, making offerings to it, adorning it, and attending upon it with respect.

Kauśika, that son or daughter of good family generates, on that basis, far greater merit. Kauśika, suppose that every being in the world-system of a great trichiliocosm were each to have built a stūpa made of the seven precious substances, each holding at its core relics of the Tathāgata. And suppose that, for as long as they lived, they honored those stūpas with divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine ointments, divine powders, divine robes, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and divine flags, with rings of divine lamps all around, and with many kinds of divine offerings; and that they showed reverence, treated them as a teacher, esteemed them, made offerings to them, adorned them, and attended upon them with respect. Let that stand.

Further, Kauśika, suppose that all the beings there are in the world-system of a great trichiliocosm were counted up, and that all of them, without exception, obtained human bodies. And suppose that each one of those beings in turn had caused to be built a stūpa made of the seven precious substances, holding relics of the Tathāgata at its core. And having had them built, suppose that each being placed all those stūpas before them and, for an eon or more than an eon, honored them with all cymbals, all songs and melodies, all dances, all music and instruments, with divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine ointments, divine powders, divine robes, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and all divine flags, with rings of divine lamps all around, and with all the many kinds of offerings of gods and humans; that they showed reverence, treated them as a teacher, esteemed them, made offerings to them, adorned them, and attended upon them with respect. And suppose that, by the merit of that very nature, all those beings had caused immeasurable and countless stūpas to be built, and had made offerings of such a nature as well.

Kauśika, what do you think? Would all those beings generate great merit on that basis?

Indra said: Blessed One, they would generate much. Sugata, they would generate much.

The Blessed One declared: Kauśika, even so, that son or daughter of good family generates far greater merit than that. It is the one who has faith in this Perfection of Wisdom, reflects on it, and is drawn to it; who, with a joyful mind, has given rise to the mind of awakening; who, with a superior intention, listens to it, upholds it, explains it, reads it, comprehends it fully, recites it, teaches it, instructs others in it, gives transmission of it, memorizes it, and expounds it extensively and correctly to others; who unfolds its meaning, contemplates it with the mind, and examines it here with wisdom as it is truly established. It is the one who does so with the thought, "May the lineage of the buddhas not be cut off; may the sublime Dharma not vanish," that is, so that the sublime Dharma may remain for a long time; and who, in a way that is not divorced from the proper manner, brings about benefit for the bodhisattvas, the great beings. And if, even in small measure, such a person has it set down in a book and keeps it, or places it in a shrine, and makes offerings to that Perfection of Wisdom with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, with rings of lamps all around, and with many kinds of offerings.

honors it, reveres it, esteems it, makes offerings to it, depicts it in paintings, and serves it with respect, then, Kauśika, that son or daughter of good family generates abundant great merit on that basis.

When the Blessed One had spoken thus, Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "So it is, Blessed One. So it is, Sugata. Blessed One, that son or daughter of good family who honors this Perfection of Wisdom, reveres it, esteems it, makes offerings to it, depicts it in paintings, and serves it with respect, will thereby have deeply honored, revered, esteemed, made offerings to, depicted, and served with respect all the buddhas, the Blessed Ones, past, future, and present, who dwell in all the world systems fully known by the buddha wisdom of the buddhas.

"Blessed One, setting aside all the sentient beings of a world system of a great trichiliocosm, consider this further, Blessed One. Suppose that in as many great trichiliocosmic world systems as there are grains of sand in the River Ganges, there were as many sentient beings as exist, and each one of those beings were to be given a stūpa of the Tathāgata, made of the seven precious substances and containing relics at its heart. And having been given these, suppose each of those beings were to place all those stūpas before them, and for an eon or longer were to make offerings with all kinds of cymbals and music, with all kinds of song, with all kinds of dance, with all kinds of instruments and rhythmic clapping, and with all divine flowers, divine incense, divine perfumes, divine garlands, divine ointments, divine powders, divine robes, divine parasols, divine banners, divine bells, and all divine flags, with rings of divine lamps all around, and with many kinds of divine offerings, honoring, revering, esteeming, offering to, depicting, and serving them with respect.

"Blessed One, this son or daughter of good family would generate far more merit than that. For such a person has firm faith in this Perfection of Wisdom, takes it up with understanding, conviction, and a clear mind, and has generated the awakening mind toward awakening. With superior intention that person listens to it, holds it, retains it, reads it, comprehends it fully, recites it, teaches it, instructs others in it, gives its transmission, and memorizes it. That person also expounds it extensively and correctly to others, explains its meaning, contemplates it in the mind as a real object, and examines it thoroughly with wisdom, according to how it is established. With the thought, 'May the lineage of the buddhas not be cut off; may the sublime Dharma not vanish,' that is, so that the sublime Dharma may remain for a long time, and in a way that is not divorced from the proper manner, that person brings about benefit for the bodhisattvas, the great beings. And if, even in small measure, such a person has it set down in a book and keeps it, or places it in a shrine, and makes offerings to that Perfection of Wisdom with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, with rings of lamps all around, and with many kinds of offerings, honoring it, revering it, esteeming it, making offerings to it, depicting it, and serving it with respect, then, Blessed One, that son or daughter of good family generates far more merit than that."

Then the Blessed One said this to Śakra, the lord of the gods: "Kauśika, so it is, so it is."

Kauśika, that son or daughter of good family generates, on that basis, a great deal of merit. Kauśika, on that basis that son or daughter of good family generates immeasurable merit. Kauśika, on that basis that son or daughter of good family generates incalculable merit. Kauśika, on that basis that son or daughter of good family generates inconceivable merit. Kauśika, on that basis that son or daughter of good family generates incomparable merit. Kauśika, on that basis that son or daughter of good family generates limitless merit.

Why is that? Kauśika, the omniscience of the Tathāgatas, the arhats, the perfectly awakened buddhas, is born from the Perfection of Wisdom, and the offerings made to the body of a Tathāgata are likewise born from omniscience.

Therefore, Kauśika, suppose a son or daughter of good family has genuine faith in this Perfection of Wisdom, reflects on it, is drawn to it, and with a clear and serene mind has generated the mind of awakening. With a superior intention, that person listens to it, holds it, retains it, reads it, comprehends it fully, recites it aloud, teaches it, instructs others in it, receives its transmission, memorizes it, and extensively and correctly explains it to others as well. That person also explains its meaning, reflects on it in the mind, and examines it thoroughly here with wisdom as it truly is. With the thought, "May the lineage of the buddhas not be severed; may the sacred Dharma not vanish," that person works so that the sacred Dharma may endure for a long time. And in order that benefit may be accomplished for the bodhisattvas, the great beings, through the Dharma not being separated from its proper manner of presentation, that person has it set down in a book and keeps it, or places it in a shrine, and makes offerings to that Perfection of Wisdom with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, with rings of lamps all around, and with many kinds of offerings. If that person honors it, reveres it, esteems it, makes offerings to it, depicts it, and serves it with respect, then, Kauśika, compared with the merit produced by honoring a stūpa of the seven precious substances that holds the relics of the Tathāgata as its core, that earlier merit does not approach even a hundredth part of this, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor a ten-millionth part, nor a hundred-ten-millionth part, nor a thousand-ten-millionth part, nor a hundred-thousand-ten-millionth part, nor even a hundred-thousandth of a vast multiple of ten million. It does not approach it in number, nor in fraction, nor in calculation, nor in analogy. It cannot be shown by comparison, and it cannot bear comparison as a basis or as a cause.

Then forty thousand sons of the gods, who had gathered in that assembly and were seated there together with Śakra, lord of the gods, said this to Śakra, lord of the gods: "Friend, take up the Perfection of Wisdom! Friend, the Perfection of Wisdom is to be taken up. Friend, the Perfection of Wisdom is to be held. Friend, the Perfection of Wisdom is to be read. Friend, the Perfection of Wisdom is to be fully comprehended. Friend, the Perfection of Wisdom is to be recited aloud. Friend, the Perfection of Wisdom is to be taught. Friend, the Perfection of Wisdom is to be explained to others. Friend, the Perfection of Wisdom is to be received through transmission. Friend, the Perfection of Wisdom is to be memorized."

Then the Blessed One said this to Śakra, lord of the gods: "Kauśika, take up this Perfection of Wisdom! Kauśika, hold the Perfection of Wisdom! Kauśika, read the Perfection of Wisdom! Kauśika, fully comprehend the Perfection of Wisdom! Kauśika, recite the Perfection of Wisdom aloud! Kauśika, teach the Perfection of Wisdom! Kauśika, explain the Perfection of Wisdom closely to others! Kauśika, receive the Perfection of Wisdom through transmission! Kauśika, memorize the Perfection of Wisdom!

"Why is this? Kauśika, whenever such a movement of mind arises among the asuras, and they think, 'Let us fight the gods of the Thirty-Three! Let us wage war together with the gods of the Thirty-Three,' then, Kauśika, you should bring to mind this Perfection of Wisdom and recite it aloud, and those very movements of mind in the asuras will subside."

When the Blessed One had spoken thus, Śakra, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, this Perfection of Wisdom is a great spell of knowledge (vidyā). Blessed One, this Perfection of Wisdom is a spell of knowledge that is immeasurable. Blessed One, this Perfection of Wisdom is a spell of knowledge that is limitless. Blessed One, this Perfection of Wisdom is a spell of knowledge that has nothing higher. Blessed One, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unsurpassed spell of knowledge. Blessed One, this Perfection of Wisdom is a spell of knowledge that has no equal. Blessed One, this Perfection of Wisdom is a spell of knowledge that is equal to the unequaled."

When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One said this to Śakra, lord of the gods: "So it is, Kauśika, so it is. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a great spell of knowledge. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a spell of knowledge that is immeasurable. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a spell of knowledge that is limitless. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a spell of knowledge that has nothing higher. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is an unsurpassed spell of knowledge. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a spell of knowledge that has no equal. Kauśika, this Perfection of Wisdom is a spell of knowledge that is equal to the unequaled.

"Why is this? Kauśika, it is in dependence on this spell of knowledge, the Perfection of Wisdom, that the buddhas of the past, the Tathāgatas, arhats, fully and perfectly awakened ones, became fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening."

Kauśika, as many tathāgatas, arhats, fully and perfectly awakened buddhas as will appear in the future, and who will become fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, all of them, Kauśika, will become fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening in dependence on this very spell of knowledge, the Perfection of Wisdom.

Kauśika, as for the blessed buddhas who at present, in immeasurable and countless world systems, the great thousand of the three thousand, are becoming fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, they too, Kauśika, become fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening in dependence on this very spell of knowledge, the Perfection of Wisdom. And I too, Kauśika, became fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening in dependence on this very spell of knowledge, the Perfection of Wisdom.

Kauśika, in dependence on this spell of knowledge, the paths of the ten virtuous actions are also made known in the world. The four meditative concentrations, which possess the factors of awakening, are made known in the world. The four immeasurables, which possess the factors of awakening, are made known in the world. The four formless absorptions, which possess the factors of awakening, are made known in the world. The six higher knowledges, which possess the factors of awakening, are made known in the world. The thirty-seven factors that lead to awakening are also made known in the world. In short, the eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma are also made known in the world. The wisdom of the buddhas, the self-arisen wisdom, and the inconceivable wisdom are also made known in the world.

This is the end of the fourth section of the Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines.

Kauśika, even at a time when tathāgatas, arhats, fully and perfectly awakened buddhas do not appear in the world, then too, Kauśika, in dependence on this very spell of knowledge, the Perfection of Wisdom, bodhisattvas, great beings, come to possess skillful means through having heard, in the past, what accords with the cause of the Perfection of Wisdom. Kauśika, those who are endowed with loving concern for sentient beings, out of that concern, rely on this world and make known in the world the paths of the ten virtuous actions. They make known in the world the four meditative concentrations that do not possess the factors of awakening. They make known in the world the four immeasurables that do not possess the factors of awakening. They make known in the world the four formless absorptions that do not possess the factors of awakening. They make known in the world the five higher knowledges that do not possess the factors of awakening.

Kauśika, it is just as, in dependence on the disk of the moon, all the medicinal herbs and stars become visible, each according to its strength and power, and the moving stars too shine, each according to its strength and power. In the same way, Kauśika, when the tathāgatas, arhats, fully and perfectly awakened buddhas have passed away and the sacred Dharma has disappeared, and when tathāgatas, arhats, fully and perfectly awakened buddhas have not appeared in the world,

Whatever practice in conformity with the Dharma, whatever peaceful practice, and whatever virtuous practice is taken up and cultivated in the world, all of it arises from bodhisattvas and is distinguished by bodhisattvas. It proceeds from the skillful means of bodhisattvas, and that skillful means of bodhisattvas should be understood as arising from the Perfection of Wisdom.

Furthermore, Kauśika, sons and daughters of good family who hold this Perfection of Wisdom, bear it in mind, read it, thoroughly understand it, recite it, teach it, explain it, expound it, memorize it, write it down, reflect on it, and remember it, may expect many benefits in this very life on that basis.

When the Blessed One had spoken thus, Śakra, lord of the gods (Indra), said to the Blessed One: Blessed One, what are the benefits in this life that those sons and daughters of good family will possess?

The Blessed One said: Kauśika, those sons and daughters of good family will not die before their time. They will not die from poison. They will not die from weapons. They will not die from fire. They will not die from water. They will not die from a staff. They will not die from harm inflicted by others. Even if a king, a prince, a great minister, or a minister should try to harm them, the harm will turn back from those who remember and recite this Perfection of Wisdom. And if any who watch for an opening or seek an opening against those who repeatedly remember and recite this Perfection of Wisdom should approach that king, prince, great minister, or minister, they will not find an opening. This is because those sons and daughters of good family are upheld by the Perfection of Wisdom.

Even when kings, princes, great ministers, or ministers come near them, they will wish to speak and converse, and will think, "I shall bring them true delight." Why is that? Kauśika, because this Perfection of Wisdom abides in the presence of all sentient beings, accomplishing loving-kindness with a mind of loving-kindness and accomplishing compassion with a mind of compassion.

For that very reason, Kauśika, when sons or daughters of good family go into a wilderness filled with many fierce beasts and venomous snakes, then humans or nonhumans who watch for an opening or seek an opening against them will find no opening, Kauśika, except through the ripening of previous karma.

Then some non-Buddhist wanderers, with the intention of finding fault, came at that time to where the Blessed One was. Then Śakra, lord of the gods, saw those non-Buddhist wanderers coming from afar, and he considered in his mind: "These non-Buddhist wanderers are coming to where the Blessed One is with the intention of finding fault. Somehow I must see to it that these wanderers do not come near to the Blessed One."

"Whatever portion of this Perfection of Wisdom I have received from the Blessed One, I shall keep in mind, reflect upon, recite from memory, and recite aloud. If I do so, there will be no obstacle to the teaching of this Perfection of Wisdom." So he thought.

Then Śakra, lord of the gods, kept in mind, reflected upon, recited from memory, and recited aloud whatever portion of this Perfection of Wisdom he had received from the Blessed One. And those other non-Buddhist wanderers, who had been roaming about, circled the Blessed One from a great distance, even farther than far, and turned back by the very gate and the very road by which they had come, and went away.

Then the venerable Śāriputra thought: "Why is it that these other non-Buddhist wanderers, from a great distance, even farther than far, circle the Blessed One and turn back by that same gate and that same road, and go away?"

Then the Blessed One, knowing with his mind the thought in the mind of the venerable Śāriputra, spoke to him in this way: "Śāriputra, Śakra, lord of the gods, saw the minds of those other non-Buddhist wanderers, who were intent on finding fault. He thought, 'It would not be right if they were to obstruct the teaching of this Perfection of Wisdom. May those other non-Buddhist wanderers not come while the Perfection of Wisdom is being taught.' So, in order to turn back those wanderers who wished to quarrel, who wished to dispute, who wished to contradict, he kept this Perfection of Wisdom in mind, reflected upon it, recited it from memory, and recited it aloud. And I too have given my approval, just as Śakra, lord of the gods, did. Why is that? Śāriputra, I have not seen a single one of those other non-Buddhist wanderers who possesses even a white, wholesome quality. Śāriputra, all of them wished to come with the intention of finding fault and with a mind of hostility."

Then the evil Māra thought: "These four assemblies of the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, are gathered and seated before the Tathāgata. And these sons of the gods who move in the desire realm and the form realm are also present. Surely here the bodhisattvas, the great beings, will be prophesied to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening. So that their eyes may not be set at ease, I shall draw near and disturb them." Then the evil Māra conjured up an army of four divisions and approached the place where the Blessed One was.

Then Śakra, lord of the gods, thought: "Alas! This is the evil Māra, who has conjured up an army of four divisions and has come to where the Blessed One is. But this array of an army of four divisions is not the array of the four-division army of King Bimbisāra. It is not the array of the four-division army of King Prasenajit. It is not the array of the four-division army of the Śākyas. It is not the array of the four-division army of the Licchavis. This has been conjured up by the evil Māra.

"The evil Māra has long been watching for an opening against the Blessed One, seeking an opportunity, and bearing ill will toward sentient beings. Now I shall reflect on this Perfection of Wisdom with mindfulness, I shall commit it to memory, and I shall recite it aloud." So he thought.

Then Śakra, lord of the gods, reflected on this very Perfection of Wisdom with mindfulness, committed it to memory, and recited it aloud. As Śakra, lord of the gods, reflected on the Perfection of Wisdom with mindfulness, committed it to memory, and recited it aloud, so the evil Māra turned back, going away by that very gate and that very road.

Then the sons of the gods of the Thirty-Three conjured up divine mandārava flowers. Remaining in the open space of the sky, they scattered those divine mandārava flowers abundantly toward the place where the Blessed One was. And they joyfully exclaimed: "Ah! This Perfection of Wisdom has appeared, after a long time, among the people of Jambudvīpa!" Then, taking up more divine flowers, they scattered them abundantly over the Blessed One, and said:

"Blessed One, those beings who explain the Perfection of Wisdom, who meditate on it, and who practice the Perfection of Wisdom will not be given an opening by Māra or by the gods of Māra's host. Blessed One, those beings who listen to this Perfection of Wisdom, who hear it and hold it, who bear it in mind, read it, fully comprehend it, recite it aloud, teach it, explain it, expound it, and commit it to memory, are not endowed with roots of virtue that are poor or lowly. Blessed One, even those beings in whose ears this Perfection of Wisdom has merely resounded have, surely, done service to the buddhas of the past. How much more so those who hold it, bear it in mind, read it, fully comprehend it, recite it aloud, teach it, explain it, expound it, and commit it to memory, and who train in accord with suchness, practice in accord with suchness, and apply themselves to yoga in accord with suchness! Blessed One, those beings have honored and attended the Tathāgata.

Why is this? Because from this Perfection of Wisdom omniscience is distinguished, and it is from this that omniscience is to be sought. Blessed One, it is just as with any precious jewels or great precious jewels whatsoever: all of these are revealed by the great ocean, and all of them are to be sought from the great ocean. In the same way, Blessed One, the great precious jewel of omniscience is to be sought from the great ocean of the Perfection of Wisdom of the Tathāgatas, the arhats, the perfectly awakened buddhas."

When they had spoken thus, the Blessed One said this to Śakra, lord of the gods: "Kauśika, so it is, so it is. The great precious jewel of omniscience of the Tathāgatas, the arhats, the perfectly awakened buddhas, is born from this great ocean of the Perfection of Wisdom."

Then the venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:

"Blessed One, you do not speak in praise of the perfection of generosity, nor do you proclaim its name far and wide. Nor that of the perfection of moral discipline, nor of the perfection of patience, nor of the perfection of diligence. Blessed One, you do not speak in praise of the perfection of meditative concentration, nor do you proclaim its name far and wide. Yet the Blessed One speaks in praise of the Perfection of Wisdom alone, and proclaims its name far and wide."

The Blessed One said: "So it is, Ānanda, so it is. I speak in praise of the Perfection of Wisdom alone and proclaim its name; I do not do so for the other perfections. Why is that? Ānanda, the Perfection of Wisdom goes before the other five perfections, and it is for this reason that they obtain the name of perfection.

"Ānanda, what do you think? Could a gift that has not been fully dedicated to omniscience obtain the name of the perfection of generosity?"

Ānanda replied: "Blessed One, it could not."

The Blessed One said: "Ānanda, what do you think? In the same way, could moral discipline that has not been fully dedicated, patience that has not been fully dedicated, diligence that has not been fully dedicated, or meditative concentration that has not been fully dedicated obtain the name of perfection? And Ānanda, what do you think? Could wisdom that has not been fully dedicated to omniscience obtain the name of the Perfection of Wisdom?"

Ānanda replied: "Blessed One, it could not."

The Blessed One said: "Ānanda, what do you think? Is the wisdom that fully dedicates all roots of virtue to omniscience inconceivable?"

Ānanda replied: "So it is, Blessed One. The wisdom that fully dedicates all roots of virtue to omniscience is inconceivable. Blessed One, it is supremely inconceivable."

The Blessed One said: "Ānanda, therefore, because it is so excellent, it obtains the name of the Perfection of Wisdom; and it is through it that the roots of virtue fully dedicated to omniscience obtain the name of perfection. Therefore, Ānanda, because all roots of virtue are fully dedicated to omniscience, the Perfection of Wisdom goes before the five perfections and leads them fully onward. In this way the five perfections are gathered within the Perfection of Wisdom alone.

"Ānanda, the term Perfection of Wisdom is a designation for the full completion of all six perfections. Therefore, Ānanda, when the Perfection of Wisdom is proclaimed, all six perfections are proclaimed.

"Ānanda, it is like this. When seeds are sown in the great earth and meet with the right gathering of conditions, they grow. The great earth is the ground of those seeds, and so it is in reliance on the great earth that those seeds grow. In just the same way, Ānanda, the five perfections, being held fully by the Perfection of Wisdom, rely on omniscience; and in reliance on the Perfection of Wisdom the five perfections come to arise. Because they are held fully by the Perfection of Wisdom, they obtain the name of perfection."

"Ānanda, therefore this very Perfection of Wisdom goes before the five perfections, and leads them, and fully guides them."

Then Śakra, lord of the gods (Indra), said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, when a son or daughter of good family takes up and holds this Perfection of Wisdom, reads it, comprehends it fully, recites it aloud, teaches it, expounds it, gives the transmission of it, and rehearses it from memory, whatever qualities such a person comes to possess, have not all those qualities of the Perfection of Wisdom been proclaimed by the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha? And yet I myself have taken up and recited only one portion of this Perfection of Wisdom, which I received directly from the Blessed One."

The Blessed One declared: "Kauśika (Indra), excellent, excellent! And yet, Kauśika, it is not only those who take up, hold, read, comprehend, recite, teach, expound, give the transmission of, and rehearse this Perfection of Wisdom to whom these qualities come. Kauśika, consider a son or daughter of good family who, thinking, 'May the lineage of the buddhas not be severed; may the sacred Dharma not vanish,' and wishing the sacred Dharma to endure for a long time, and so that benefit may be accomplished for bodhisattvas, the great beings, without departing from the proper way, writes out this Perfection of Wisdom, places it in a book, and holds it or keeps it. That person honors that Perfection of Wisdom with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, cloth, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, with rings of lamps all around, and with many kinds of offerings. They show it reverence, regard it as their teacher, esteem it, make offerings to it, adorn it with paintings, and attend upon it with respect.
